column1: # S. R. Rao 1982, The Decipherment of the Indus Script (Asia Publishing House, Bombay). Transcribed 2026-10-18 from the
# archive.org scan "jlus-the-decipherment-of-the-indus-script-s-r-rao-engli" (uploader-declared CC0; book itself not redistributed here).
# language: sa (Rao: "old Indo-Aryan"). Sources inside the book: Fig. 4/4A (pp. 36-37, basic linear signs with seal refs),
# Fig. 8 (p. 41, phonetic value of common Semitic and Indus signs), Fig. 9 (p. 42, classification), Fig. 10 (p. 43, vowels,
# short strokes as vowel indicators), Fig. 11-13C (pp. 47-52, compound signs). ICIT ids assigned by eye against the lipi font
# glyph sheet of the 200 commonest corpus signs. confidence: sure = shape unambiguous; likely = shape matches but a near twin exists.
# Rao's own transcription is kept (ś, ṛ, ḥ, ḫ, ə, ā); run49.common() collapses it. Signs not confidently matched are omitted
# (notably his logosyllables aśva/śakunta/kṣetra/makṣa and most compounds of Fig. 11-13C).
